universal_patterns.pattern: any holder of a license[^.]*under this (?:article|title)

proposal.rationale: New York's umbrella occupational licensing statute is Education Law Title 8 (The Professions), with Article 130 providing general provisions that apply to all subsequent profession-specific articles (131-165+). NY uses "Article" as its primary subdivision (Justia slugs look like "article-130"), so slug_prefix is "article" and chapter_cite_pattern captures article numbers (including hyphenated forms like "139-A"). Section citations in NY Education Law for the professions use 4-digit section numbers where the first two digits identify the article (e.g., § 6500 = Article 130 introductory; § 6700s = Article 131 Medicine; § 6800s = Article 131-B Physician Assistants, etc.) — group 1 captures those leading two digits as the article/chapter token. Universal patterns are kept narrow: "this article applies to any/every/all", license-holder language tied to "this article/title", and subarticle variants. The bare "as used in this article" is intentionally omitted because Article 130 is the umbrella and that phrase alone is too broad — the cross-state AS_USED_RE will handle the legitimate cases. Trigger patterns cover the standard "licensed to practice / licensed under / licensed pursuant to" phrasing used to enumerate practice-act articles.
